readout.note: single <Z0> through a scalar scale and bias - one logit, binary by construction

circuit.name: tree
circuit.bonds: the disjoint pairs (0,1), (2,3), ... of the active register only
circuit.block: 8 shared angles per round: RY and RZ on each wire, CNOT(a, b), then RZ and RY on each wire
circuit.pooling: CRY from the discarded wire onto its kept partner, 1 shared angle per stage; an odd register's last wire is pooled into the first
circuit.simulability: a tree of two-qubit blocks: after every pooling stage the survivors are a product of one-qubit states, so it is classically simulable in linear time at any width

provenance: IBM AMLworld HI-Small (Altman et al., NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks; Kaggle, CDLA-Sharing-1.0, https://cdla.dev/sharing-1-0/), SYNTHETIC transactions; the published MLP's temporal windows, the fit window's every laundering transaction and four others each; 8 of the 114 inputs, chosen on the fit window by |AUC - 0.5|: format_risk, pair_log_same_direction, pair_first_contact, dst_in_uniq_4320, dst_bank_diversity, src_out_uniq_60, src_out_mean_60, src_out_mean_360.

training.device_name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition
training.note: --seed drives the numpy split permutation and torch parameter init. Re-running this command on a CUDA device regenerates theta, scale, bias and every metric bit for bit: five consecutive runs of each Round 47 artifact, and two independent runs of each Round 84 one (for medical and telecom the pre-registered experiment and the retrain, for finance the four-column retrain and a repeat of it), max |diff| 0. That is true only since the multiclass readout stopped using index_add_, whose CUDA atomicAdd made the same seeded command land on macro F1 0.809846 or 0.807781 depending on the run. On a CPU it is not guaranteed: CPU and CUDA kernels differ in float rounding, and a long multiclass run amplifies that.

classical_surrogate.model: logistic regression on the 6561 Pauli products of the same encoded angles, same split, same estimator as the raw comparator
classical_surrogate.threshold: the score maximising validation minority-class F1, as the circuit's

note: Variational QCNN trained by backpropagation through a dense state vector. The prediction path applies NO QOTP mask: undoing a Pauli frame through Clifford+T is not implemented here (T X T-dagger is not Pauli), so hiding and prediction are kept separate rather than claiming a correction that does not exist. Simulated, not hardware; the classical baseline above is reported so no quantum advantage is implied. SERVED (Round 86, batch 6): the fit window's standardisation folded into feature_mean and feature_std, and the validation-best threshold into the bias; see `standardisation`, `decision_threshold` and `clip_effect`.

selection.rule: the highest validation average precision of arm 1's twenty seeds (the comparison's criterion 1)

decision_threshold.rule: the logit maximising minority-class F1 on the validation window (710,969 transactions), the comparison's own rule; never chosen on the test window

standardisation.folded: the fit window's centre and scale of each input, from scripts/data/aml_qcnn_inputs.py, are this file's feature_mean and feature_std; the trainer's input was the same standardised value clipped at 10, and the clip is not carried (see `clip_effect`)

replaces: the PaySim QCNN of Round 84 (four wires, PaySim's four columns), which the finance page ran until 2026-11-26
